name: Set the example
definition: As Marines progress through the ranks by promotion, all too often they take the attitude of "do as I say, not as I do." Nothing turns Marines off faster! As a Marine leader, your duty is to set the standards for your Marines by personal example.

rows.situation: When you ask the team for a standard
rows.under: Asks for a standard you do not keep yourself.
rows.justRight: Keeps the same standard in your own work, then asks it of them.
rows.over: Performs the standard so loudly that the work becomes a show about you.

rows.situation: When a shortcut would be convenient for you
rows.under: Takes the shortcut and tells them not to.
rows.justRight: Does the step you asked them to do, including the unglamorous one.
rows.over: Refuses every convenience, including ones that do not touch the standard, to look stricter than the team.

rows.situation: When people are watching how you handle a hard week
rows.under: Lets the week show as complaint, lateness, or a drop in care.
rows.justRight: Holds appearance, attitude, and follow-through at the same bar you set on a calm week.
rows.over: Performs stamina and will not name a real limit, so they hide theirs too.

rows.situation: When you want an exception you would not give them
rows.under: Takes the exception and hopes they do not notice.
rows.justRight: Applies the same rule to yourself, or changes the rule for everyone.
rows.over: Denies yourself a reasonable exception to make a point, and the team learns the rule is theater.

rows.situation: When the standard is easy to skip in private
rows.under: Keeps the standard only when someone will see it.
rows.justRight: Does the same work the same way when the room is empty.
rows.over: Audits yourself in public so often that the point becomes being seen.
